description:
Project: CosmosKisaan Challenge: Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data

CosmosKisaan bridges the gap between NASA Earth data and rural Indian farmers. Using a multilingual WhatsApp AI bot, we deliver agronomic insights with 1 click—no heavy apps or fast internet needed. By integrating NASA's SMAP (soil moisture), HLS (crop health), and GPM (weather) datasets, we translate complex satellite telemetry into simple, actionable local-language alerts to help optimize crop yields.
summary:
CosmosKisaan bridges the gap between complex NASA Earth data and rural Indian farmers by translating heavy satellite telemetry into simple, 1-click insights delivered directly through a multilingual WhatsApp AI bot.

Traditional farming in India faces severe disruptions from climate change, unseasonal rainfall, and droughts. While NASA monitors global environmental metrics daily, this vital intelligence remains locked behind high-bandwidth requirements and complex file formats that rural farmers cannot access. CosmosKisaan eliminates these barriers through a zero-friction platform requiring no heavy apps, fast internet, or technical literacy.

The platform integrates critical NASA open datasets, including SMAP for real-time soil moisture monitoring, HLS for tracking vegetative health and crop stress via NDVI, and GPM and NASA POWER for hyper-local precipitation and weather forecasting. When a farmer shares a location pin on WhatsApp, the backend processes these data streams and responds instantly in their native language with actionable advice—such as when to irrigate or avoid applying fertilizer before unseasonal rain.

Designed for scalability and economic feasibility, CosmosKisaan empowers independent farmers with space-age data to protect their crops and secure food production.
details:
What does it do or how does it work? CosmosKisaan bridges the gap between complex NASA Earth observation data and rural Indian farmers by translating heavy satellite telemetry into simple, 1-click insights delivered directly through a multilingual WhatsApp AI bot. Farmers share a location pin on WhatsApp, use quick-reply buttons (e.g., "Check Soil"), and instantly receive regional language advice.

What benefits does it have & intended impact? It eliminates internet, hardware, and language barriers. By providing real-time alerts for soil moisture, crop stress, and unseasonal rainfall, it helps farmers optimize irrigation, protect crops, and secure yields without needing technical training or heavy app downloads.

Tools, coding languages, hardware, and software used:

  • Frontend: React, Tailwind CSS, Leaflet.js (for the agronomist map dashboard).
  • Backend: Python (FastAPI), LangChain for LLM integration.
  • APIs / Data Sources: NASA SMAP (soil moisture), HLS / Sentinel-2 (NDVI crop health), and GPM / NASA POWER (meteorological forecasting).
  • Communication: Twilio Sandbox for WhatsApp interactive messaging.

Creativity & Considerations: Instead of building yet another web dashboard that rural farmers cannot access, we flipped the user experience by using WhatsApp—an existing, highly trusted infrastructure. We balanced economic feasibility with advanced space tech, ensuring zero device storage or onboarding costs for independent farmers.
